lesson.evidence: FFD and exact pairing both achieved 6 bins (theoretical minimum). Random ordering with first-fit produced 7 bins in 10 of 12 seeds (83%), with only 2 seeds finding the optimal 6-bin solution. Items form perfect complementary pairs (8+2, 7+3, 6+4) filling capacity-10 bins exactly. Worst random case placed small items together (birch+jade+frost=9) leaving large items isolated.
lesson.statement: Random first-fit packing is unreliable for perfectly complementary items: only 17% of seeds achieved optimal packing versus 100% for weight-based ordering (FFD).

summary: Compared FFD, exact pairing, and 12-seed random first-fit.
All items form complementary pairs summing to capacity 10.
FFD and exact pairing achieved optimal 6 bins immediately.
Random ordering found optimum in only 2 of 12 trials.
Final solution: 6 bins, all exactly filled to capacity.
